gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-glegoo: Sealed-up, city-hard letters up top, no stroke variation to soften them. Glegoo then lets its curves swing wide open, a text serif with a lowercase that feels refined and editorial beside such a tight-lipped heading.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-headland-one: Capture It stacks its towering, nearly sealed letters into a commanding heading with no weight shifts at all. And Headland One, a serif with dignified, well-spaced letters and gently varying strokes, would feel oddly delicate if the heading were shrunk down beside it.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-hedvig-letters-: Hedvig Letters Serif brings open-ended curves and a sturdy lowercase, with contrast you only notice on a close look. But Capture It, with its nearly sealed shapes and curves that never thin at the shoulders, stays the louder voice over pages of that steady text.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-kadwa: Commanding and urban, Capture It barely lets any light in. Kadwa, a classic serif with open-ended curves and a generous x-height, loosens the page with an editorial ease, as its diagonals and strokes there never bulk up like the heading's.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa spills its counters into the surrounding space, giving words a sturdy, large look next to the sealed, constant-width strokes of Capture It. Over a long page it stays solid and readable, with only mild stress.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-marcellus-sc: Marcellus SC reads gently, with soft stroke modulation and pulled-back terminals. Capture It is best at hammering out towering, single-thread urban headlines, while the classic serif body does its quiet, dignified, literary work in stem-to-serif weight shifts.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-serif-hent: Noto Serif Hentaigana keeps open jaws on every curve and small letters nearly as high as capitals. Size it up a little for comfort, since its modulation is subtle, while Capture It's hairline-free strokes hold up on their own.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-ovo: Authoritative from the first line, Capture It runs a marker-like constant stroke with barely any openings. Ovo, a serif whose joins thin gently without turning spindly, adds a deep middle band and spacious curve terminals that give the pair its strongest quality: heft with breathing room.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-scope-one: Blunt, sealed-up capitals-in-waiting: that's Capture It, with no weight shift along any curve. Scope One, the classic serif here, is the one that spills counters outward and tucks stubby ascenders and descenders around a big x-height.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-gf-noto-serif-: Raw, chunky lowercase leads in Capture Smallz, built big-bodied and tactical. But Noto Serif Hentaigana would drown it if the heading went small and the body large, since its arches thin slowly into lighter joins.
